items.note: android/gradlew.bat and android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml are present, so the project is buildable in principle. Nothing can compile or launch without the SDK and a JDK. Installing them is a multi-gigabyte toolchain install on the owner machine and is the owner’s decision, not a step to take unasked mid-task.

An Xcode project exists. iOS cannot build on Windows at all, so this depends entirely on macOS CI, which needs an authenticated gh. Two device codes have already expired unused. Owner action: gh auth login.

The requirement is tapping approve and deny on a phone and observing the real PC-side effect. There is no connected device; adb is not even installed to detect one. A simulated tap would proved nothing, and dressing one up as a real approval would be exactly the kind of false green this contract forbids.
Same device dependency as K2, against a live PC task.
Needs a real push notification to arrive on a real device and a phone on a genuinely different network reaching this PC through a deployed relay. None of the three is available here.
